report.question: For every detector, gate, validator and probe in the program, does it FIRE on a known-broken input and stay SILENT on a known-good input - or is it silent in both states and therefore measuring nothing?
report.headline: 17 detectors, 18 both-states pairs. 17 pairs are VALID (fires on broken, silent on good). EXACTLY ONE is DECORATIVE: tools/command-center/validate.py's V-FIELDS check under the bare invocation CI uses - and that one is the unit's own mandated meta-control, so the audit passed its calibration case rather than failing it. Zero FALSE-POSITIVE-MACHINEs were found.
report.meta_control_outcome: PASS - D01 classified DECORATIVE (silent-in-both), which is what the unit requires. Had this audit classified it VALID, the audit itself would be broken and every other verdict here would be void.

harness_defects_caught.wrong_reading: fires in BOTH states (would have been reported as a false-positive machine)
harness_defects_caught.actual_cause: the GOOD fixture held 60 tracked .json files, below jsonparse's own declared floor of 800, so the tool's fail-closed check fired on the good state too. Raising the fixture to 900 files gave (0, 1) = VALID.
harness_defects_caught.lesson: a GOOD fixture below a tool's own fail-closed floor manufactures a false 'fires-in-both'.

harness_defects_caught.wrong_reading: exit 2 on the bad state, then fires in BOTH states
harness_defects_caught.actual_cause: attempt 1 pointed python at a directory with no refcheck.py ('can't open file' - not a detector reading at all); attempt 2 used a 1-reference fixture, below refcheck's own floor of 12. 15 references gave (0, 1) = VALID.
harness_defects_caught.lesson: a non-zero exit is not automatically a 'fire' - read the output before scoring it.

harness_defects_caught.wrong_reading: silent in BOTH states (would have been reported as a second decorative gate)
harness_defects_caught.actual_cause: the rival fixture defined 'reduce_claims'/'ClaimState', which are NOT in reducer.py's BANNED_DEFINITIONS = {evaluate, CONDITIONS, CONDITION_TEXT, NON_WAIVABLE}. A rival defining CONDITIONS/NON_WAIVABLE/evaluate was caught at rival.py:3, giving (0, 1) = VALID.
harness_defects_caught.lesson: a plausible-looking broken fixture is not a broken fixture; derive it from the detector's own rule table. This was one step from becoming a fabricated second finding - the same class this unit audits.
